result.reasoning:
REFUTED. The finding is a docstring-completeness nit with zero numeric consequence, and the reporter concedes it ("No wrong output results"). Review scope here is defects that change numbers or conclusions; comments/docstrings are explicitly out of scope. Beyond that, three concrete facts cut against it, two of which I verified by hand:

(1) Implementation matches the implied contract exactly, everywhere I could push it. /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/opus_semistd_pos_doc/check.py re-implements `sqrt(mean(max(log(x[t]/x[t-1]),0)^2))` with the n>=3 rule in plain numpy, straight from the suggested docstring text, and compares against `cross_semistd_pos` / `cross_semistd_neg` (partura/ops_ext.py:676-700) on: random positive price panels at every grid window (3/5/10/15/30/60/241); panels with suspensions, a zero, a negative, a late listing, a delisting and scattered holes; and columns sitting exactly on the n=2 vs n=3 boundary. 26/26 checks: max|diff| <= 1.4e-17, zero NaN-pattern mismatches. Nothing to reproduce.

(2) The "upstreaming one function in isolation" premise is false for this pair. /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/docs/new_operators.md:62 documents them as one joint row — "`cross_semistd_neg(x, d)` / `…_pos` | 正值序列日度对数变化的下行(上行)半标准差" — so the very document whose process the finding invokes already treats neg/pos as a single item.

(3) The one machine-read channel for these docstrings makes the finding backwards. /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/semantics.py:215 renders only `d.doc.splitlines()[0]` into the operator dossier that main researchers read. Verified output: neg renders as the truncated fragment 'Downside semi-deviation of the daily log change of a positive ``x`` over the last' — losing both the formula and the NaN rule — while pos's one-line docstring renders complete. Applying the suggested change would push pos into the same truncation, i.e. make the channel that actually feeds downstream decisions strictly worse.

The strongest version of the finding would be "an agent misreads the operator and produces a bad factor". That has happened (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/handoff/TOOLING.md:115 records agents feeding a signed series `day_close(Ret)` into cross_semistd_*, cov dropping to 0.21), but the failure there was the positive-series precondition, which pos's docstring does state ("of a positive ``x``"). The omitted parts — the closed form and the n>=3 threshold — are not implicated in any observed misuse.

result.corrected_fix: Not needed (no defect in scope). But if anyone does edit the docstring, do NOT paste the suggested sentence verbatim: "NaN with fewer than 3 such days", sitting directly after "max(log(x[t]/x[t-1]), 0)", reads as "days whose log change is positive", which is wrong. The kernel's n counts valid day pairs (both x[t] and x[t-1] finite and > 0) regardless of the change's sign; wrong-sign pairs are clamped to 0 and still count toward n. Verified: a strictly falling column with 4 valid pairs and zero up-days returns 0.0, not NaN. cross_semistd_neg (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/ops_ext.py:690) carries the same slight imprecision ("fewer than 3 days" where the code means 3 day pairs). Correct wording for either side, e.g.: "Upside semi-deviation of the daily log change of a positive ``x`` over the last ``d`` days: ``sqrt(mean(max(log(x[t]/x[t-1]), 0)^2))`` over the day pairs where both values are finite and positive (negative changes count as 0, and still count); NaN with fewer than 3 such pairs." Note that /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/semantics.py:215 keeps only the first line, so any added formula must fit on line 1 or it will be dropped from the dossier agents read — which is the stronger reason to leave pos's one-liner alone and instead shorten neg's first line.
